main_text.p: caremoniis,idololatriis,incantationibus, exorcif-mus, sputis, legendis,vitis,fabulis,ocijs,ineptijs, atq; aliis innumeris apostaticarum adinuentionū impostuṙis & abominationibus. Pro his perda-moniorum doctrinas firmandis, ac per disceptā-tiones sophisticas perpetuandis, Robertus D.Lu-douici Francorum regis frater,his temporibus Pa-risiorum Sorbonam primus instituit. Et alter eius frater, Alphonsus, Pictauensium comes, minis ac terroribus pios doctores per Domicanos fuga-bat. Et ut Cantipratensis habet in opere suo de A-pibus mysticis, Albertus Magnus, Hugo Cardina-lis, Thomas Aquinas, Bonauentura, & alij eiusdē farinæ theologi, mirabilia magna et multa Parisijs tunc faciebant. Philosophiam quoq; qua deinceps in scolis utebantur magistri nostri, Erasmus dicit in quadam ep stola, his diebus esse natam. Degenerabant istis temporibus (inquit Lelandus) a sua pu-ritate artes, unā cum Latinæ linguæ elegantia: per strepebatq; in scholis nescio quæ sophistica garrulitas. Eos igitur omnes, quibus Seruator Christus cordi est, adhortor in Domino, ut hæc ob ea quæ in Ecclesiæ doctrinis ac doctoribus deinceps usq; ad annum Domini 1520. sequuntur, medullitus hoclo-co perpendant, explorent, iudicent.

page.notes: Lines 8 to 11 and parts of lines 6 and 16 show slanted or underlined type. I could not decide with certainty which words are italic, so the italic marking is partial. Two small ornamental marks stand in the left margin beside "cordi" and "Ecclesiæ"; they are not text and were not transcribed as notes. The catchword at bottom right is cut off by the page edge and reads "mu" with uncertainty. The printed line ends "septi-" at the foot of the page, and the word continues on the next page. Long s has been written as a plain s throughout.
